inherited_methods.method: The predecessor proof assigns point-private prime blocks only to the points and lines of PG(2,q).
inherited_methods.loss_step: The proof invokes projective-plane regularity before the prime-block path is constructed, although the path argument uses only a bound on the number of incident edges at each point.
inherited_methods.lost_information: Distinct nontrivial bipartitions of one prime block can encode the incident edges of any finite hypergraph vertex once the block size is logarithmic in its degree.
inherited_methods.consequence: The recorded theorem appears tied to a single incidence host and does not expose the reusable embedding mechanism.

inherited_methods.method: The predecessor collision proof uses the fact that two projective points determine a unique projective line.
inherited_methods.loss_step: Projective geometry is used where the proof only needs that no pair of vertices lies in two different host edges.
inherited_methods.lost_information: The exact hypothesis is linearity of the host hypergraph; it is sufficient to prevent collisions between private two-block values on different edges.
inherited_methods.consequence: The incidence-fidelity statement can extend from projective planes to all finite simple linear hypergraphs.

inherited_methods.method: Support minimality is stated only for coefficients in {-1,0,1}.
inherited_methods.loss_step: The odd-prime row on each path edge actually propagates an arbitrary rational or integral kernel vector, not only a cancelled subrelation.
inherited_methods.lost_information: The prime-valuation kernel is one-dimensional and generated by the primitive alternating vector, so every relation is a circuit in the integer-matrix sense.
inherited_methods.consequence: The predecessor statement understates the algebraic minimality and its relation to primitive partition and toric-circuit theory.

inherited_methods.method: The predecessor computes tau and nu directly for PG(2,q).
inherited_methods.loss_step: Private path vertices are treated as a special nuisance rather than as vertices of degree one that can always be replaced by a shared host vertex from the same edge.
inherited_methods.lost_information: Adding edge-private vertices preserves both matching number and transversal number for every nonempty host hypergraph.
inherited_methods.consequence: Any admissible linear host's matching-transversal gap transfers exactly to the arithmetic relation family.

required_new_information: A host-uniform prime-budget lemma in terms of the number of vertices, maximum degree, a prime cutoff B, and the bit scale K.
A padding proof for variable edge sizes m_e>K with an explicit decrement vector, its exact sum, its maximum entry, and the resulting equality of two-adic exponents.
A full valuation-kernel proof showing that the alternating relation is a primitive integer circuit.
An incidence-fidelity proof for arbitrary simple linear hosts and exact transfer arguments for the edge-intersection graph, matching number, and transversal number.
